edits.html:
Vaccines at the Infant Visits

Well infant, vaccines up to date · which vaccine the age allows at this visit

Source vignette Pt — 4-month-old girl at a well-child visit in October; uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery; immunizations up to date; normal growth, development, vital signs and examination · Q — immunization against which disease is most appropriate now; options spanned chickenpox, influenza, measles-mumps-rubella, rotavirus and shingles
The decision point

At 4 months, an infant who is up to date gets the second doses of the 2-month vaccines. These are DTaP (diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and acellular pertussis), Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b), PCV (pneumococcal conjugate vaccine), IPV (inactivated poliovirus vaccine) and oral rotavirus vaccine. Rotavirus vaccine has fixed age limits: the first dose by 14 weeks 6 days and the last dose by 8 months 0 days.

Influenza vaccine starts at 6 months, so an October visit does not make a 4-month-old eligible. MMR (measles-mumps-rubella) and varicella vaccines are live vaccines first given at 12 to 15 months. Zoster vaccine is an adult vaccine, given from age 50.

Defining criteria: age limits Rotavirus — first dose by 14 weeks 6 days, final dose by 8 months 0 days; 2 doses at 2 and 4 months (RV1, monovalent rotavirus vaccine) or 3 doses at 2, 4 and 6 months (RV5, pentavalent rotavirus vaccine) · Influenza — from 6 months, every season; a child aged 6 months to 8 years with fewer than 2 earlier doses gets 2 doses at least 4 weeks apart · MMR and varicella — first doses at 12 to 15 months, second doses at 4 to 6 years · Recombinant zoster — 2 doses 2 to 6 months apart from age 50, or from age 19 with immunocompromise
Vaccines due at each infant visit
VisitVaccines dueAge limit that matters here
2 monthsDTaP, Hib, PCV, IPV and rotavirus, first doses; hepatitis B second dose if not given at 1 monthRotavirus must start by 14 weeks 6 days
4 monthsDTaP, Hib, PCV, IPV and rotavirus, second dosesToo young for influenza (6 months) and for MMR and varicella (12 months)
6 monthsDTaP and PCV third doses; Hib third dose except with the PedvaxHIB product; rotavirus third dose with RV5 only; IPV and hepatitis B third doses (due 6 to 18 months); influenza in seasonRotavirus series ends by 8 months 0 days; the first influenza season needs 2 doses
12 to 15 monthsMMR and varicella first doses; hepatitis A first of 2 doses (12 to 23 months); PCV fourth dose; Hib boosterRoutine MMR and varicella start at 12 months
Scenario bank
Schedule status, September 2026 In January 2026 the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) moved childhood rotavirus and influenza vaccines from routine to shared clinical decision-making. A federal court stayed that change in March 2026, and the stay is under appeal. The schedule CDC now posts is the 2025 schedule, which lists both vaccines as routine; check the CDC site for the current schedule. The AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) schedule also keeps both routine, and this NBME item keys rotavirus as a routine 4-month vaccine.
Pearls Rotavirus vaccine is live and oral; do not give it with SCID (severe combined immunodeficiency) or after an intussusception · Up to date at 4 months means the 2-month doses were given, so the second doses are due · Older sources, including this NBME explanation, start zoster vaccine at 60; recombinant zoster vaccine is now given from 50
How NBME framed it The October date is a seasonal cue for influenza, but at 4 months she is below its 6-month age limit. The options form an age ladder of live and inactivated vaccines, from rotavirus at 2 months through MMR and varicella at 12 months to zoster at 50.
Pairs with Aquifer Adolescent Immunization and the Age Platform covers the 11 to 12 year visit and influenza timing by season. Part I DTaP: Contraindication vs. Precaution covers when a DTaP dose is withheld. Ask: has this child reached the vaccine's age window, and has the window closed?
Transferable rule Check the child's age against each vaccine's age window before the season or the disease. A vaccine whose window has not opened, or has closed, is not given at this visit.
Unchecked attributeChickenpox: a routine live childhood vaccine; the first varicella dose is not given until 12 months.
Salient decoyInfluenza: the October visit falls in influenza vaccine season; she is 4 months old, and influenza vaccine starts at 6 months.
Unchecked attributeMeasles-mumps-rubella: routine and live, like rotavirus; the first dose is at 12 months.
Unchecked attributeShingles: the same virus as chickenpox; zoster vaccine is for adults from age 50.
